post_title: Looking for a good SEO agency for early-stage SaaS
post_body: We've tried two so far and neither understood the product-led growth side. Anyone had luck?
reply: The trick with SaaS SEO is finding an agency that gets programmatic pages and topical clusters, not just keyword lists. What worked for us was hiring one that had shipped for at least two other SaaS companies in similar ARR range — happy to share who if useful.

post_title: What's the best lead-gen tool right now?
post_body: Apollo feels stale. Clay is cool but expensive. Looking for something in between.
reply: Honestly it depends on your workflow — if you're doing high-volume outbound, Apollo's data is still fine. If you're building signal-based sequences, Clay is worth the price. There's also a middle-ground category worth looking at that handles enrichment + Reddit intent together in one place.

post_title: Need to hire a python dev for automation work
post_body: Small scraping + Airtable sync project, few days of work. Where do I even look?
reply: For a few-days project like that Upwork or r/forhire will get you decent options. If you want higher quality with less filtering, ping a couple of people from GitHub who've built similar things — most freelance devs will do a small project on the side. Good luck!

post_title: Just started a Shopify store, completely lost
post_body: Need help with theme setup, apps, and initial products. Where do I hire someone?
reply: Been in that exact spot — Shopify's overwhelming when you first open it. Look for a 'Shopify Expert' on their official directory (they're vetted). For a full setup you'll typically pay $500-1500. Don't overthink apps at the start; ship with the basics, add complexity when you have real customers.

post_title: Instantly vs Smartlead — which is better for cold email in 2026?
post_body: Sending about 500 emails/day, need good deliverability and inbox rotation.
reply: At 500 emails/day both will work, but the deliverability difference comes down to how well they handle warmup and inbox rotation. Test each with a small campaign on your own domain and compare open rates over two weeks — the winner will be obvious. Also worth considering the price/feature ratio if you scale beyond 1000/day.

post_title: Looking for a reliable YouTube video editor
post_body: Weekly 10-15 min videos in the finance niche. Budget flexible for the right person.
reply: For finance content specifically, look for editors who've worked with other finance/business YouTubers — the pacing and B-roll style is very different from lifestyle or gaming. Best bet is scouting the credits on channels with similar production quality to yours and reaching out to those editors directly.

post_title: Need help building a Notion workspace for my team of 8
post_body: We use Google Docs currently and it's chaos. Where do I find a Notion expert?
reply: For a team of 8, you probably want someone who's set up Notion for teams before (not just individual power users — the multiplayer patterns are different). Notion's own consulting directory has vetted experts; you can also find good ones in the Notion Ambassadors community on their forum.

post_title: Recommendations for a bookkeeper who specializes in small SaaS
post_body: Founded my SaaS 6 months ago, revenue is picking up and I'm behind on the books.
reply: For SaaS specifically, look for someone familiar with deferred revenue and subscription accounting — a generalist bookkeeper will fumble this. Pilot and Bench are the well-known options but they can get pricey. A solo bookkeeper who specializes in SaaS is often better value if you can find one.

post_title: Need a logo designed for my new SaaS. Budget $300-500
post_body: Any designers you'd personally recommend? Not looking for Fiverr quality.
reply: For that budget you can get solid work from designers on Dribbble or 99designs contests. If you want to skip the contest pain, DM designers directly whose portfolios you like — many will do a one-off logo project even if their main business is bigger brand work. Look for ones who explicitly list SaaS/tech clients.

post_title: Migrating off Mailchimp — what's the best alternative in 2026?
post_body: About 8k list, mostly ecommerce. Mailchimp pricing is getting ridiculous.
reply: For ecommerce at 8k subscribers, Klaviyo is the go-to — the Shopify integration alone justifies the switch. If your list is more content-driven than transaction-driven, ConvertKit (now Kit) is cheaper and simpler. Whichever you pick, budget a full weekend for the migration; the segment mapping is where most people underestimate the effort.

post_title: Looking to hire someone to build a small chrome extension
post_body: Simple extension that adds a sidebar to Gmail. Any recommendations on where to find good devs?
reply: Chrome extension work is a fairly specialized skill — good bet is searching GitHub for open-source extensions with clean code and reaching out to those authors. Most will take a small paid gig. Toptal and Arc are decent for higher-budget projects; for smaller one-offs, Upwork with strict filtering on past chrome extension work is fine.

post_title: Hiring a graphic designer for ongoing social media assets
post_body: About 10 hours/week for Instagram, LinkedIn, and email templates.
reply: For that volume you want a designer on a monthly retainer, not one-offs — much better velocity. Look for someone with an existing SaaS or marketing portfolio; they'll get the constraints faster. Rates are usually $30-60/hr for solid mid-level work depending on turnaround expectations.

post_title: My WordPress site loads slowly — any consultants who specialize in this?
post_body: Site is on a decent host but page-load is 5+ seconds. Losing rankings.
reply: WordPress performance work is a mix of hosting, plugin audit, image optimization, and JS/CSS management. Most 'general WP consultants' can't do all four well — look specifically for someone who mentions Core Web Vitals as their focus. Kinsta and WP Engine both maintain lists of vetted specialists. Expect $500-1500 for a proper end-to-end optimization.

post_title: Need a copywriter who's good at cold email specifically
post_body: Not blog posts, not landing pages — actual cold outreach that gets replies.
reply: Cold-email copy is a niche and most general copywriters are bad at it. Best bet is finding someone who currently runs their own outbound and knows their reply rate. Check who's active in the sales-focused communities (Pavilion, RevGenius) — those folks are usually happy to take one-off copy gigs.

post_title: Anyone use tools to monitor Reddit for sales leads?
post_body: Manual searching is a huge time sink and I'm sure I'm missing 90% of the conversations.
reply: This exact problem is what I built for — the manual searching + tab-hopping is genuinely brutal. Whatever you pick, make sure it does two things: (1) actually understands intent (not just keyword match) and (2) reads comments not just posts, since a lot of the highest-intent buying signals show up as replies under other people's threads.
